h: Holy Eating Holds the Key to the Whole Torah

p: In Midrash Tanchuma (on this parshah, Tazria 1)
it appears that it explains the juxtaposition
and it writes: "So too this infant,
before it has come out of its mother's womb,
מִזֶּה תֹּאכַל וּמִזֶּה לֹא תֹּאכַל כוּ׳
'From this you may eat and from this you may not eat,' etc."
And so it is in the Gemara (Niddah 30b).
וּמְלַמְּדִין אוֹתוֹ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כּוּלָּהּ כוּ׳
"And they teach it the entire Torah, etc.,
all the mitzvos in the Torah,
So why did it single out,
of all the mitzvos in the Torah,
specifically the matter of forbidden foods?
And the root of the serpent's incitement
was to bring desire into eating;
and one who is restrained in eating,
as a matter of course keeps
all the mitzvos in the Torah;
for the yetzer hara has dominion
"And you will eat and be satisfied.
and as they said in the Sifrei there
And it is stated in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 24)
the Rabbis of the Mishnah said:
The tree from which Adam HaRishon ate
and others say it was a vine, etc.;
and they did not disagree in their words,
for all of it is true, etc."
But how can it be conceived that all is true
when they disagree about the facts?
And we said that in truth it is written (Bereishis 2:9):
"And the Tree of Life in the midst of the garden,"
that is, the inner aspect of all the trees of the garden
and the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil;
he would have sensed in all eating
the taste of the Tree of Life,
לְכוּ לַחֲמוּ בְלַחְמִי וְגוֹ׳ (מִשְׁלֵי ט, ה)
And when he ate from the Tree of Knowledge,
then he sensed in all eating
the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil
(and this was explained in Bereishis, maamar 48);
and this is the root of the corruption.
so that eating is in holiness,
then as a matter of course he keeps all the mitzvos
and is saved from the accusation of the yetzer hara.
when the eating of Yisrael is in holiness,
"He who keeps the Shabbos from profaning it
and keeps his hand from doing any evil,"
that he merits to be guarded from sin,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמְּכִילְתָּא (בְּשַׁלַּח, מַסֶּכְתָּא דְּוַיַּסַּע ו)
as they said in the Mechilta (Beshalach, Vayassa 6);
and in Pri Etz Chaim the wording is
that he is saved from the accusation of the yetzer hara.
and it is stated in the holy Zohar (Terumah, Zohar II 154b)
that the eating of the Lechem HaPanim on Shabbos is effective
into all the eating of the kohanim, even on weekdays,
that they be saved from the accusation of the yetzer hara.
And this is what it says:
כְּשֶׁמְּצַוֶּה אוֹתוֹ אֶת זֶה תֹּאכַל כוּ׳
when He commands it, "This you may eat, etc."
that its eating be in holiness,
for in this all the mitzvos of the Torah are included.
is equal to all the mitzvos,
as they said in the Midrash
if you will listen to His voice" (Tehillim 95:7)
as referring to keeping the Shabbos day;
and so it is written in the holy Zohar
That is, on the Shabbos day
the eating of a Jew is in holiness,
and all the mitzvos are included in this,
for his eating is words of Torah:
